name: Metaphysics and Epistemology
solves: test a general claim against a possible case
say how belief should change with evidence

tools.name: Method of cases (thought experiment)
tools.does: tests a principle against a described case
hypotheses: the judgement about the case is shared or defended

tools.name: Bayesian conditionalisation
tools.does: updates degrees of belief on new evidence
hypotheses: prior degrees of belief obey the probability axioms
the evidence is learned with certainty

notes: drafted in session by a model from general knowledge; no source checked; needs specialist review

name: Value Theory
solves: bring principles and judgements about cases into agreement
choose under uncertainty in a consistent way

tools.name: Reflective equilibrium
tools.does: adjusts principles and case judgements until they fit
hypotheses: both the principles and the judgements are open to revision

tools.name: Expected utility theory (von Neumann–Morgenstern)
tools.does: represents consistent preferences as maximising expected utility
hypotheses: preferences over lotteries are complete and transitive

notes: drafted in session by a model from general knowledge; no source checked; needs specialist review

name: Science, Logic, and Mathematics
solves: decide whether a conclusion follows from premises
say when an observation supports a hypothesis

tools.name: First-order logic
tools.does: tests validity of arguments by formal proof
hypotheses: the argument can be expressed in a first-order language

tools.name: Bayesian confirmation
tools.does: says evidence supports a hypothesis when it raises its probability

tools.name: Falsification
tools.does: tests a hypothesis by a prediction that could fail
hypotheses: the hypothesis yields a testable prediction

notes: The logical theorems are owned by MA. Drafted in session by a model from general knowledge; no source checked; needs specialist review

name: History of Western Philosophy
solves: establish what an author meant in a text

tools.name: Charitable exegesis
tools.does: reads a text so that its argument is as strong as the words allow
hypotheses: the historical context is taken into account
